title: How to hide cursor in Cursor on Mac: a guide for distraction free coding
metaTitle: How to hide cursor in Cursor on Mac: Easy Guide
description: Learn how to hide cursor in Cursor on Mac. Since the editor lacks a native setting, use these macOS tools for a clean, distraction free coding workspace.
intro: There is no built-in setting to hide the mouse cursor within the Cursor editor on your Mac. You must use a third-party macOS utility or system-level behaviors to achieve a clean, distraction free coding environment.
tldr: Cursor does not offer a native hide cursor feature.
Download Cursorcerer to toggle cursor visibility with a global keyboard shortcut.
Use macOS full screen mode to hide the cursor automatically in many cases.
Avoid patching the editor binary to prevent corruption warnings.

blocks.text: Why Cursor lacks a hide cursor setting

The Cursor editor is built on the VS Code framework. It inherits the core architecture and limitations of that platform. Neither VS Code nor Cursor includes a native toggle to hide the mouse cursor while typing or reading code. This design choice assumes the mouse is always required for interaction, even though many developers prefer to keep their screen clear while focusing on deep work.

Many users attempt to find this feature in the settings menu. You will not find it there. Some community extensions attempt to patch the editor workbench. These often trigger a warning stating that your installation appears to be corrupt. It is best to avoid these patches. They break frequently when the editor updates.

Cursorcerer is the standard tool for Mac users who need to hide the cursor. It is a lightweight utility that runs in the background. It works system-wide, meaning it hides your cursor in Cursor, Chrome, Slack, or any other app you use. It is compatible with Apple Silicon and the latest versions of macOS.

items: Download the latest version of Cursorcerer from the official site.
Install the application and grant the necessary accessibility permissions in System Settings.
Open System Settings and locate the Cursorcerer panel at the bottom of the left sidebar.
Assign a global hotkey, such as ⌥ ⌃ K, to toggle visibility.
Configure an idle timer if you want the cursor to disappear automatically after a set period.

blocks.text: Alternative methods for a clean workspace

If you do not want to install a utility, you can rely on standard macOS behaviors. When you put Cursor into full screen mode, the menu bar and dock disappear. Moving your mouse to the far edge of the screen often triggers the system to hide the cursor in certain contexts, though this is not as reliable as a dedicated utility.

Some developers use the keyboard to navigate entirely. By using the command palette with ⌘ ⇧ P or the file search with ⌘ P, you can keep your hands on the keyboard. This reduces the need to reach for the mouse. When your hand is not on the mouse, the cursor is less of a distraction.

If you choose a hotkey that is already in use by Cursor or another app, you will experience conflicts. For example, ⌘ K is the primary shortcut for inline edits in Cursor. Do not use this for your cursor hiding utility. Check your System Settings under Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts to ensure your chosen key combination is free.

rows: Use a three-key combo like ⌥ ⌃ ⇧ H
blocks.caption: Avoid common keyboard shortcut conflicts between system utilities and Cursor.

blocks.text: What to do when the cursor reappears

The cursor will reappear the moment you touch your trackpad or move your mouse. This is normal. If it reappears without your input, check if you have a secondary input device connected. A loose connection on a wired mouse or a low battery in a wireless mouse can cause jitter. This jitter registers as movement and forces the cursor to become visible again.

Hiding the cursor is part of a larger strategy to maintain focus. Many developers also disable line numbers, hide the minimap, and collapse the file explorer. You can do this in the Cursor settings under View > Appearance. Combining these visual changes with a hidden cursor creates a terminal-like experience within the modern IDE.

faq.question: Can I hide the cursor natively in Cursor?
faq.answer: No. Cursor is based on VS Code and does not include a native setting to hide the mouse cursor.

faq.question: Will Cursorcerer break my editor?
faq.answer: No. Cursorcerer is a system-level utility. It does not modify the Cursor application files, so it will not cause corruption warnings.

faq.question: How do I make the cursor disappear automatically?
faq.answer: Use the idle timer feature in Cursorcerer. You can set it to hide the cursor after 3 to 15 seconds of inactivity.

steps.name: Download Cursorcerer
steps.text: Visit the official Cursorcerer website and download the latest version for your Mac.

steps.name: Configure accessibility
steps.text: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility and add Cursorcerer to the list of allowed apps.

steps.name: Set your hotkey
steps.text: Open the Cursorcerer menu in System Settings and define a global hotkey to toggle cursor visibility.

steps.name: Test the hide function
steps.text: Return to Cursor and press your chosen hotkey to verify the cursor disappears.
